name: IEC three-state buffer (rectangular form)
summary: IEC buffer whose output carries the three-state triangle and is controlled by an EN input.
description: The three-state buffer is drawn as a 1 element with a small downward triangle inside the outline next to the output, and an EN input. When EN is at its internal 1 state the output follows the input; at its internal 0 state the output goes to its external high-impedance state while the internal logic state is retained.

These elements appear where several drivers share a bus, such as data lines between controller cards. The drawing should make clear which signal drives each EN input and how the design prevents two drivers being enabled together, since the symbol itself does not show arbitration.

A negated EN input means the enable is active low, which is how many devices are supplied. Read the input marking carefully; reversing the enable sense would put a buffer on the bus at the wrong time.
readingNotes: Find the EN input and check its polarity.
Identify all other drivers on the same bus.
drawingChecklist: Place the three-state triangle next to the output.
Label the EN input and its source.
Show bus contention protection or a note on enable sequencing.
distinction: An open-circuit output uses a diamond qualifier and has no high-impedance logic state of its own; the three-state triangle is different.
